translationRepairs: During the Xiahou time, some were lost and some continued.
During the time of the Xia rulers, some were lost and some continued.
夏后 denotes the Xia ruling house (Xia rulers), not a personal or clan name Xiahou; the proposed wording restores that sense.
In the fifteenth year, Duke Ling drank with his two sons at the Xia clan.
In the fifteenth year, Duke Ling drank with the two men at the Xia clan.
In the preceding unit 靈公以告二子, 二子 are the officers Kong Ning and Yi Xingfu, not Duke Ling's sons; the repair removes the false kinship.
The two men said: 'He also resembles you, my lord.'
二子 again names those two officers, and 公 is the duke addressed as 'my lord,' not a transliteration 'gong'; the proposed sentence is accurate.
Eight generations after, none rival with Jing.'
After eight generations, none will rival them in greatness.
莫之與京 uses 京 as 'to rival in greatness,' not a personal name Jing; the replacement correctly restores the oracle formula.

In the seventh year, the three younger brothers of Crown Prince Mian of Duke Huan, whom Duke Li had killed—the eldest named Yue, the middle named Lin, the youngest named Chu Jiu—together commanded the Cai people to lure Duke Li with beautiful women, and together with the Cai people killed Duke Li and established Yue, who became Duke Li.

In the seventh year, the three younger brothers of Crown Prince Mian of Duke Huan, whom Duke Li had killed—the eldest named Yue, the middle named Lin, the youngest named Chu Jiu—together commanded the Cai people to lure Duke Li with beautiful women, and together with the Cai people killed Duke Li and established Yue, who became Duke Ligong.

厲公 and 利公 are distinct titles both often rendered Duke Li; the proposal rightly marks the accession title, but the English field cannot embed Chinese characters, so Ligong disambiguates in Latin script.
Having executed Xia Zheng Shu, he therefore suspended Chen and possessed it. All the ministers congratulated him.
Having executed Xia Zheng Shu, he therefore made Chen a county and took possession of it. All the ministers congratulated him.
縣陳 is the verbal use of 縣, 'make Chen a county,' not 'suspend'; the proposed wording matches the annexation sense.
In the twenty-ninth year, Chen doubled-crossed the Chu alliance.
In the twenty-ninth year, Chen betrayed the Chu alliance.
倍楚盟 means Chen turned against/betrayed the Chu covenant; 'doubled-crossed' is a misleading calque of 倍.
Light thousand chariot state but heavy one word.'
He treated lightly a state of a thousand chariots but valued a single word.'
The telegraphic literal drops the agent and obscures the 輕/重 contrast of valuing a word above a thousand-chariot state; the repair restores grammatical English without changing sense.
Zhao what killed Dao crown prince, crown prince's son named Wu, fled Jin.
When Zhao killed the Dao crown prince, the crown prince's son named Wu fled to Jin.
招之殺悼太子也 is a topical 'when Zhao killed Crown Prince Dao' clause; 'Zhao what killed' misreads 之, and 出奔晉 needs 'fled to Jin.'
Ping Wang first ascended, desired obtain harmony feudal lords, then sought former Chen Dao crown prince Shi's son Wu, established as Chen Hou, this was Hui Gong.
When Ping Wang first ascended, he desired to obtain harmony among the feudal lords; he then sought Wu, son of the former Chen Dao crown prince Shi, established him as Chen Hou—this was Hui Gong.
The original literal is ungrammatical telegraphic English; the proposed wording restores clause structure while preserving 平王, 悼太子師, 陳侯, and 惠公.

When King Ping had just ascended, he wished to restore harmony among the feudal lords, so he sought out Wu, the son of the former Crown Prince Shi of Duke Dao of Chen, and established him as lord of Chen. This was Duke Hui.

When King Ping had just ascended, he wished to restore harmony among the feudal lords, so he sought out Wu, the son of Chen's former Crown Prince Dao Shi, and established him as lord of Chen. This was Duke Hui.
故陳悼太子師 is Chen's former Crown Prince Dao (name Shi); 'Duke Dao of Chen' invents a ruler the Chinese does not name.
Qi Dong Lou Gong was Xiahou Yu's descendants posterity.
Qi Dong Lou Gong was a descendant of Yu of the Xia rulers.
夏后禹 is Yu of the Xia rulers, and 之後苗裔 is singular descendant language; 'Xiahou Yu's descendants posterity' is both ungrammatical and misnames 夏后.
Duke Ping died in his eighteenth year. His son Duke Dao Cheng Li ascended.
Duke Ping died in his eighteenth year. His son Duke Dao Cheng ascended.
悼公成 gives posthumous title Duke Dao and personal name Cheng only; the invented 'Li' has no source in the Chinese.
Qi's descendants became Yin. Yin has basic annals that speak of this.
Xie's descendants became Yin. Yin has basic annals that speak of this.
契 is the Shang ancestor Xie; rendering him as 'Qi' wrongly conflates him with the state 杞 treated in neighboring sentences.
Yin was broken. Zhou enfeoffed their descendants at Song. Duke Min of Qi extinguished them. There are hereditary houses that speak of this.
Yin was broken. Zhou enfeoffed their descendants at Song. King Min of Qi extinguished them. There are hereditary houses that speak of this.
齊湣王 is explicitly a king (王), not a duke; correcting to King Min restores the title.
King Hui of Chu extinguished Qi. His descendants' King Gou Jian of Yue rose.
King Hui of Chu extinguished Qi. Later, King Gou Jian of Yue rose.
其后 is temporal 'afterward,' not 'his descendants'; the original invents a kinship between King Hui of Chu and King Gou Jian of Yue.
candidateDispositions: Chen clan 陳氏, not an individual
七月 is a calendar month, not a person
Yu in 'Tang and Yu' is the Tang-Yu era label (唐虞), not a personal name distinct from Shun/Yu enumeration
